astb-01-c2.text: Carlos Mariscal; Bruce Weber (2021). Life. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
astb-01-c2.quote: Consider NASA's operational definition of life as "a self-sustaining chemical system capable of Darwinian evolution" (Joyce 1994).
astb-01-c2.claim: life is a self-sustaining chemical system capable of Darwinian evolution

astb-02-c2.text: Michael Gillon, Amaury H. M. J. Triaud, Brice-Olivier Demory, Emmanuel Jehin, Eric Agol, et al (2017). Seven temperate terrestrial planets around the nearby ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1. Nature 542, 456–460 (arXiv).
astb-02-c2.quote: Our observations reveal that at least seven planets with sizes and masses similar to the Earth revolve around TRAPPIST-1.
astb-02-c2.claim: TRAPPIST-1 (announced 2017 by Michael Gillon and team) hosts seven Earth-sized planets

astb-06-c2.text: David S. McKay, Everett K. Gibson Jr., Kathie L. Thomas-Keprta, Hojatollah Vali, Christopher S. Romanek, Simon J. Clemett, Xavier Chillier, Claude R. Maechling, Richard N. Zare (1996). Search for past life on Mars: possible relic biogenic activity in martian meteorite ALH84001. Science (New York, N.Y.).
astb-06-c2.quote: could thus be fossil remains of a past martian biota
astb-06-c2.claim: In 1996, David McKay and a NASA Johnson team published in Science that it contained nano-scale magnetite chains, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and segmented carbonate globules they interpreted as fossil Martian microbes.
